signals.name: regexSteps
signals.quantity: count of Pattern$Node.match() invocations during regex matching — each call is one NFA state transition or backtracking step in the regex engine
signals.storage: ThreadLocal<long[]> in RegexStepCounter.counter; counter.get()[0] holds the running count per thread
signals.reset: RegexStepCounter.reset() called at the start of V1Guidance.getInput() before providing the next input
signals.read: RegexStepCounter.get() called in V1Guidance.handleResult() to retrieve the step count

plans.retention: Primary: retain inputs with the highest regexSteps value in a corpus of up to 20 entries sorted by step count. When a new execution yields a step count exceeding the current corpus minimum, it replaces the minimum-scoring entry. Secondary (when regexSteps is flat across all corpus entries): retain inputs that are longer (trending toward 10240 bytes) or that contain more dictionary tokens (@, ., -, etc.) to reach code on the attack path. This ensures the search makes progress toward the target input_bytes even when the step-count signal is constant.
mutation: Byte-level: random byte flip, byte insertion, byte deletion, byte overwrite at random positions

Repetition (R45a): select a random chunk (1 byte to half the input length) and repeat it k times in place, with k chosen to fill up to 10240 bytes; includes whole-input doubling. Grows from 16-byte seed to 10240 bytes in ~10 doublings (<1 second).

Dictionary (R45b): tokens from the v7 regex source on the attack path: '@' (0x40, email separator), '.' (0x2E, domain label separator), '-' (0x2D, valid in domain/local), '+' (0x2B, valid in local), '_' (0x5F, valid in local), '\n' (0x0A, affects $ anchor). Inserted or overwritten at random positions.
No encoder needed (R45c): input is plain UTF-8 text, no format constraints.
